name: nshm23_wus
source: nshm-conus active-crust/fault branch-averaged WUS fault system solution (2023 NSHM)
notes: Collapsed (branch-averaged) model; weights are normalized together with the other active crust fault system models. Distances as in nshmp-lib (SystemRuptureSet, model.Distance.compute): fault_distances "nshmp_grid" builds the nshmp-lib DefaultGriddedSurface of each section (1 km grid; aseismicity removes the top of the plane) from sections.npz and takes rJB and rRup as the minimum distances to its grid points (top row only for dip > 89), with rJB = 0 if less than the grid spacing and inside the section perimeter (which nshmp-lib builds from the trace, i.e. without the aseismic shift of the top), and rX from the top row extended 1000 km along strike (section_rx "extended_trace" gives the same rX from the rectangles of "triangles" distances). The rupture rRup is the minimum over its sections, rX is that of the section with the smallest rRup, and rJB is the minimum over its sections; nshmp-lib takes the rJB minimum over only the 4 sections with the smallest rRup, which differs in rare cases (0.02% of the rate within 50 km of Los Angeles), not reproduced.
